description: STRIDE-per-element baseline threat enumeration rules for architecture model snapshots (GC-GRC-007). Covers STRIDE baseline (one rule per element-kind × stride-category), trust-boundary crossing threats, external-entity data flows, secrets/crypto/pipeline metadata tags, and data-egress flows.

threatRuleEntries.title: External Entity: Spoofing
threatRuleEntries.narrativeSkeleton: External entity {{element}} may be spoofed. An attacker can impersonate the external actor, causing the system to accept malicious input or forge its identity in downstream operations.
threatRuleEntries.rationale: External entities are outside the trust boundary and their identity cannot be verified by the system directly.

threatRuleEntries.title: External Entity: Repudiation
threatRuleEntries.narrativeSkeleton: External entity {{element}} may repudiate its actions. Without non-repudiation controls, the external actor can deny sending requests or performing actions.
threatRuleEntries.rationale: External entities are not under organisational control; actions taken must be logged and attributable.

threatRuleEntries.title: Process: Spoofing
threatRuleEntries.narrativeSkeleton: Process {{element}} may be spoofed. An attacker can impersonate this process to receive or inject data intended for a legitimate component.
threatRuleEntries.rationale: Processes communicate over channels that may be intercepted; their identity must be authenticated.

threatRuleEntries.title: Process: Tampering
threatRuleEntries.narrativeSkeleton: Process {{element}} may be tampered with. An attacker with local access or code-injection capability can modify process state or logic.
threatRuleEntries.rationale: Processes are subject to code injection, memory corruption, and configuration tampering.

threatRuleEntries.title: Process: Repudiation
threatRuleEntries.narrativeSkeleton: Process {{element}} may perform operations that are later denied. Without adequate audit logging, repudiation of high-value operations is possible.
threatRuleEntries.rationale: Processes must log security-relevant operations with sufficient attribution to support non-repudiation.

threatRuleEntries.title: Process: Information Disclosure
threatRuleEntries.narrativeSkeleton: Process {{element}} may disclose sensitive information. Errors, logs, or inter-process communication can leak data to unauthorised parties.
threatRuleEntries.rationale: Processes may expose sensitive data through verbose error messages, debug output, or insecure IPC.

threatRuleEntries.title: Process: Denial of Service
threatRuleEntries.narrativeSkeleton: Process {{element}} may be disrupted by a denial-of-service attack. Resource exhaustion or crash-inducing inputs can render the process unavailable.
threatRuleEntries.rationale: Processes are subject to resource exhaustion, crash loops, and algorithmic complexity attacks.

threatRuleEntries.title: Process: Elevation of Privilege
threatRuleEntries.narrativeSkeleton: Process {{element}} may be exploited to elevate privileges. A vulnerability in this process could allow an attacker to gain higher privileges than intended.
threatRuleEntries.rationale: Processes running with elevated privileges are high-value targets for privilege-escalation attacks.

threatRuleEntries.title: Component: Spoofing
threatRuleEntries.narrativeSkeleton: Component {{element}} may be spoofed. An attacker can present a counterfeit component to intercept or forge communications.
threatRuleEntries.rationale: Components expose APIs or interfaces that must authenticate callers and verify their own identity.

threatRuleEntries.title: Component: Tampering
threatRuleEntries.narrativeSkeleton: Component {{element}} may be tampered with. Supply-chain attacks or runtime injection can modify component behaviour.
threatRuleEntries.rationale: Components (libraries, services, microservices) are subject to supply-chain and runtime tampering.

threatRuleEntries.title: Component: Repudiation
threatRuleEntries.narrativeSkeleton: Component {{element}} may perform actions that are later denied. Insufficient logging prevents attribution of security-relevant operations.
threatRuleEntries.rationale: Components must emit structured audit events for security-relevant operations.

threatRuleEntries.title: Component: Information Disclosure
threatRuleEntries.narrativeSkeleton: Component {{element}} may disclose sensitive information through its interfaces, error responses, or telemetry.
threatRuleEntries.rationale: Components expose APIs and emit telemetry; both are potential information-disclosure vectors.

threatRuleEntries.title: Component: Denial of Service
threatRuleEntries.narrativeSkeleton: Component {{element}} may be made unavailable by resource exhaustion or malformed input.
threatRuleEntries.rationale: Components are subject to request floods, large-payload attacks, and algorithmic complexity exploits.

threatRuleEntries.title: Component: Elevation of Privilege
threatRuleEntries.narrativeSkeleton: Component {{element}} may be exploited to execute operations beyond its intended privilege level.
threatRuleEntries.rationale: Components with broad permissions are high-value targets for privilege escalation via injection or misconfiguration.

threatRuleEntries.title: Data Store: Tampering
threatRuleEntries.narrativeSkeleton: Data store {{element}} may be tampered with. An attacker with write access can modify stored records, corrupting data integrity.
threatRuleEntries.rationale: Data stores are the persistence target for tampering attacks; integrity controls are required.

threatRuleEntries.title: Data Store: Repudiation
threatRuleEntries.narrativeSkeleton: Data store {{element}} may be modified without an audit trail, enabling repudiation of data changes.
threatRuleEntries.rationale: Data stores must maintain tamper-evident audit logs for compliance and forensic analysis.

threatRuleEntries.title: Data Store: Information Disclosure
threatRuleEntries.narrativeSkeleton: Data store {{element}} may expose sensitive data to unauthorised parties through direct access, backups, or queries.
threatRuleEntries.rationale: Data stores often hold the most sensitive data in a system and are a primary target for exfiltration.

threatRuleEntries.title: Data Store: Denial of Service
threatRuleEntries.narrativeSkeleton: Data store {{element}} may be made unavailable through resource exhaustion, locking, or destructive queries.
threatRuleEntries.rationale: Data stores are subject to table-lock attacks, quota exhaustion, and destructive DELETE/DROP operations.

threatRuleEntries.title: Data Flow: Tampering
threatRuleEntries.narrativeSkeleton: Data flow {{element}} may be tampered with in transit. A man-in-the-middle attacker can modify data passing through this channel.
threatRuleEntries.rationale: Data flows are subject to interception and modification without transport-layer integrity protection.

threatRuleEntries.title: Data Flow: Information Disclosure
threatRuleEntries.narrativeSkeleton: Data flow {{element}} may disclose sensitive data to eavesdroppers without encryption.
threatRuleEntries.rationale: Unencrypted data flows expose all data in transit to network-level interception.

threatRuleEntries.title: Data Flow: Denial of Service
threatRuleEntries.narrativeSkeleton: Data flow {{element}} may be disrupted, preventing legitimate communication between components.
threatRuleEntries.rationale: Data flows can be blocked or flooded, preventing system components from communicating.

threatRuleEntries.title: Trust Boundary: Elevation of Privilege
threatRuleEntries.narrativeSkeleton: Trust boundary {{element}} may be bypassed to obtain elevated privileges. An attacker who crosses this boundary gains access to a higher-trust zone.
threatRuleEntries.rationale: Trust boundaries define the attack surface between security domains; boundary enforcement must be verified.

threatRuleEntries.title: Trust Boundary: Spoofing
threatRuleEntries.narrativeSkeleton: Trust boundary {{element}} may be spoofed. A component in a lower-trust zone could present itself as originating from a higher-trust zone.
threatRuleEntries.rationale: Trust boundaries require mutual authentication to prevent identity spoofing across security domains.

threatRuleEntries.title: External Source Flow: Authentication Bypass
threatRuleEntries.narrativeSkeleton: Data flow {{element}} originates from an external entity and may lack adequate authentication. An unauthenticated external actor could spoof an authenticated identity.
threatRuleEntries.rationale: Flows from external entities require authentication controls to prevent identity spoofing.

threatRuleEntries.title: External Source Flow: Privilege Escalation via Missing Authorization
threatRuleEntries.narrativeSkeleton: Data flow {{element}} carries requests from an external entity. Insufficient authorisation checks may allow the external caller to access privileged operations.
threatRuleEntries.rationale: External actors must have their permissions explicitly verified before accessing protected resources.

threatRuleEntries.title: Trust-Boundary-Crossing Flow: Untrusted Input
threatRuleEntries.narrativeSkeleton: Data flow {{element}} crosses a trust boundary. Input traversing this boundary must be validated; unvalidated data can corrupt downstream state.
threatRuleEntries.rationale: Data crossing trust boundaries is untrusted by definition and must be validated before processing.

threatRuleEntries.title: External Target Flow: Data Egress Risk
threatRuleEntries.narrativeSkeleton: Data flow {{element}} sends data to an external entity. Uncontrolled egress to an external party risks information disclosure if the recipient is compromised or malicious.
threatRuleEntries.rationale: Outbound flows to external entities are a primary exfiltration vector and require data-loss-prevention controls.

threatRuleEntries.title: Secret-Tagged Process: Secret Leakage
threatRuleEntries.narrativeSkeleton: Element {{element}} ({{elementKind}}) handles secrets. Improper secret management — in memory, logs, or transit — can expose credentials or keys.
threatRuleEntries.rationale: Elements tagged as handling secrets require hardened secret-management controls to prevent credential exposure.

threatRuleEntries.title: Crypto-Tagged Element: Cryptographic Weakness
threatRuleEntries.narrativeSkeleton: Element {{element}} ({{elementKind}}) performs cryptographic operations. Weak algorithms, improper key management, or implementation flaws can allow tampering with cryptographic outputs.
threatRuleEntries.rationale: Cryptographic components require algorithm agility, proper key rotation, and validated implementations.

threatRuleEntries.title: Crypto-Tagged Element: Key/Algorithm Disclosure
threatRuleEntries.narrativeSkeleton: Element {{element}} ({{elementKind}}) performs cryptographic operations. Hardcoded keys, weak randomness, or side-channel leakage can expose cryptographic material.
threatRuleEntries.rationale: Cryptographic material exposed through side-channels or logging represents a critical information-disclosure risk.

threatRuleEntries.title: Pipeline-Tagged Element: Supply-Chain Tampering
threatRuleEntries.narrativeSkeleton: Element {{element}} ({{elementKind}}) is part of the deployment pipeline. A compromised pipeline component can inject malicious code or configuration into all downstream deployments.
threatRuleEntries.rationale: Pipeline components have write access to the build and deploy artefacts; tampering here has cascading downstream impact.

threatRuleEntries.title: Pipeline-Tagged Element: Elevated Pipeline Privileges
threatRuleEntries.narrativeSkeleton: Element {{element}} ({{elementKind}}) is part of the deployment pipeline. Pipeline components often run with elevated credentials; a compromised pipeline element can leverage these privileges.
threatRuleEntries.rationale: Deployment pipelines require elevated access by design; that privilege must be strictly scoped and audited.
